title: ACP event envelope (ACP-1.1 amendment candidate implementation)
description: Machine-checkable contract for a single ACP event envelope. Layer: Implementation. Scope: ACP Core semantics only. STATUS: implementation of ACP-1.1 as published in feat/acp-1-1-normative-amendments@1bda3e997291e337cc1a3956462e643219d71547. ACP-1.1 is itself an amendment candidate that has not been approved, so this schema is an AMENDMENT CANDIDATE IMPLEMENTATION, not a conformant implementation of an adopted standard. Conformance requires format-assertion to be enabled in the validator (see README, Conformance requirements). Syntactic validity here is necessary but NOT sufficient: see README, What this schema cannot validate.

v.description: ACP Core version as major.minor (ACP-1.1 section 16.1). THIS SCHEMA IS WRITER-STRICT FOR ACP-1.1 AND ACCEPTS EXACTLY 1.1. It rejects 1.0 (structurally different: no mandatory actor, no subject rule), 1.2 and any later minor (their semantics are not implemented here, and validating them against 1.1 rules produces a confusing false rejection on unknown members), the old integer form, and non-canonical spellings such as 01.1. Reader tolerance towards a later minor is a SEPARATE layer, not this file (ACP-1.1 section 16.2): a future minor needs a future schema.

program.description: Programme identifier. Subject of an event that belongs to no item thread. Exactly one of item or program is required (ACP-1.1 section 5.2.1, amendment A17).

actor.description: declared_actor: the logical identity the event CLAIMS. Mandatory on every authored event (ACP-1.1 section 8.6, amendment A10). The observed identity is produced by the platform and lives in the binding record, never in the authored envelope; the binding compares the two and raises violation:identity-mismatch. THIS FIELD DOES NOT ASSERT AUTHENTICITY. Below profile identity.trust_level 3 it is an unverifiable label.

on_behalf_of.description: The principal when the author is operating for someone else (ACP-1.1 section 8.6 rule 5, amendment A22). actor is who operates; on_behalf_of is who answers for it. Capabilities are NOT inherited from the principal: they are checked against actor.

after.description: Causal predecessor: the platform-assigned identifier of the last event of this thread the author had read. Generated by the PLATFORM, never by the author (invariant I4). Mandatory unless the event declares itself a root.

root.description: Declares this event as the first of its thread, which is the only admissible reason to omit `after`. Explicit rather than inferred from absence: under ACP, silence never carries meaning. Only root-eligible types may set it (see $defs/rootEligibleType).

oneOf.$comment: A17: every event names exactly one subject. Neither, or both, is violation:unscoped-event.

allOf.$comment: A11: an event that mutates work item state cannot silently omit its causal predecessor.

A root event declares no predecessor and must be of a type that can legitimately begin a thread. risk, debt and violation were root-eligible in schema 0.2.0 and are NOT in ACP-1.1: each is always discovered while doing something, and dropping the link loses where.
L4 / ACP-1.1 section 5.4.1: decide may be a root only when its subject is a programme. A decision about an item continues a thread and must link to it.

eventType.description: Closed catalogue. 24 types are normative in ACP-1 section 5.3; risk, debt and revalidate are amendment candidates A2 and A3, reconciling section 5.3 with sections 6.3, 13.2, 13.3 and Appendix A.
eventType.$comment: CATALOGUE PARITY (conformance requirement C1): this enumeration is duplicated in profile.schema.json#/$defs/eventType. Both copies MUST carry the same catalogue digest below, which is the sha256 of the comma-joined sorted list with no spaces. Comparing two digest strings is a one-glance check; diffing two 27-item lists is not. catalogue-digest: sha256:046f7cadad317948c7a92a808bade47bbbdf61bdb467ce26a49891da730e0e91

rootEligibleType.description: Types that may legitimately begin a thread with no causal predecessor (ACP-1.1 section 5.4.1). Three, not six: spec creates an item thread; reconcile may open a programme thread; decide may begin one only when programme-scoped. risk, debt and violation always link to existing history, because each is discovered or incurred while doing something and the link is half of its value.

protocolVersion.description: A protocol version as major.minor in the grammar of ACP-1.1 section 21, with no leading zeros. Used by checkpoint from/to, where any released version may be named, unlike the v of an authored event which this writer-strict schema pins to 1.1.

programId.description: Programme identifier. Like a work item identifier, Core requires only a stable opaque token; the concrete shape is profile policy.

entityId.description: Identifier of a risk, debt or decision record. Core imposes NO prefix pattern (L3): RSK-, DEBT- and ACD- are profile policy (profile.ids.risk_prefix, debt_prefix, decision_prefix). Core only requires a stable opaque token.

extensions.description: Single container for local extensions (ACP-1.1 section 5.2.3, amendment A14). Keys match ^x-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$; values may be any JSON. A container rather than loose x- members at the root, so that 'an extension cannot shadow a normative field' is structurally true instead of a rule to police. Anything that merely looks like an extension (X-Foo, x-, x_foo) is not one. A tolerant reader MUST preserve extensions it does not understand.

workItemId.description: Core requires only that a work item identifier be a stable, opaque, printable token: non-empty, bounded, no whitespace, no control characters. Core deliberately imposes NO naming policy. Prefixes, patterns and reserved identifiers are profile-normative (profile.schema.json: ids.work_item_prefix, ids.work_item_pattern, ids.reserved). Consequence, stated plainly: this schema alone will accept an identifier that a given programme forbids, such as one colliding with a product roadmap namespace. Rejecting it requires validating the envelope against the active profile as a second pass. That is the price of not baking one organization's naming into a universal Core, and it is the right price.

actorId.description: Stable logical identifier of an agent or human. Core does not define the mapping from actorId to a platform account: that is binding-normative and is the weakest link in the trust model.

fullSha.description: Exactly 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Abbreviated SHAs are rejected: they are ambiguous across repositories and over time, and an anchor that can become ambiguous cannot support invalidation. This tightens the grammar in ACP-1 section 21, which permitted a 10-character prefix.

digest.description: Content digest of evidence output, normalized before hashing.

ref.description: Branch or tag name. Only a conservative character set is checked. Full git reference legality, and whether the ref exists, are semantic concerns.

repository.description: Portable repository reference. Core does not know what owner/name means: that is one platform's convention, and encoding it here would make every non-GitHub binding a second-class citizen. A reference names the version-control system and carries an opaque or URI identifier the binding knows how to resolve. The GitHub shorthand belongs in the binding: { system: git, id: https://github.com/owner/name.git }, or in an x- member.

id.description: Opaque identifier or URI, resolvable by the binding. Not parsed by Core.

causalPointer.description: Reference to a platform-assigned event identifier, in the canonical namespaced form <binding>-<class>:<id>, for example github-comment:2451889301 (ACP-1.1 section 5.4.1, amendment A21). The bare integer accepted by schema 0.2.0 is gone: outside its platform it means nothing, and one of the points of the log is that it can be read from outside. The identifier is produced by the PLATFORM; an author copies it and never constructs, deduces or recalls it.

eventRef.description: Something the protocol can point at exactly: an event or an entity.

duration.description: Relative duration. Permitted units: h (hours), d (days), w (weeks). Minutes and months are deliberately absent: minutes are below the granularity of an agent turn, and months are ambiguous in length. All ACP deadlines are relative because the authoritative clock is the platform's event timestamp, not the agent's (ACP-1 invariant I4).

timestamp.description: Absolute RFC 3339 instant. NOT admissible for expires, lease or ttl in any envelope: those are relative by invariant I4. Provided for entity records (for example a decision record's decided date) and for informative free text only.

basis.description: Content anchor of an assertion. sha is mandatory: an assertion without a full SHA cannot be invalidated, therefore ACP treats it as inadmissible for any gate.

base.description: Structured base pointer. Replaces the ACP-1 string form main@a71c0e94, which cannot be validated as a pair.

depends.description: Entity versions this assertion depends on. Movement of any of them makes the assertion SUSPECT (rule R3).

scope.description: Paths the assertion actually covers. Enables the revalidate shortcut when a later diff falls outside it.

environment.description: Where the assertion was produced. Omitting it is how a correct observation becomes a false conclusion.

touches.description: Declared write surface. Non-empty and duplicate-free so that overlap between concurrent work items is a set intersection. A bare wildcard is not forbidden but cannot be silent: see the touches_rationale rule on spec and claim.

wildcardOnlyTouches.description: Helper predicate: true when the declared surface contains a pattern that claims everything.

uncertaintyDeclaration.description: Explicit statement of what the author did NOT verify (ACP-1.1 invariant I5, amendment A19). The KEY is mandatory where the event type requires it; an EMPTY ARRAY is admissible and means 'nothing left to verify'. Absence and emptiness are not the same thing: 0.2.0 required at least one entry, which forced authors to invent an uncertainty in order to deliver. An empty declaration is a strong claim and the adversarial reviewer should attack it. No minimum length on entries, on purpose: a threshold is satisfied by padding and converts a substantive obligation into a formatting one. Whether entries are truthful and material is semantic.

falsification.description: What the reviewer tried to break and what happened. Required of adversarial reviewers: absence of found defects is not evidence of absence unless someone states what they attacked.

evidenceReference.description: A reproducible observation. cmd and env are mandatory: without the command it cannot be repeated, and without the environment a true observation can support a false conclusion.

modifier.description: Orthogonal flag. Parameterized modifiers carry their target after a colon.

state.description: Composite state. Phase advances, freshness is derived from the basis, modifiers are orthogonal and never move the phase.

resume.description: Transferable context packet. Every key is mandatory; empty arrays are legal. Requiring the key while permitting emptiness forces an explicit answer without inviting invention: 'no traps' is information, a missing traps key is not.

traps.description: Negative memory: what has already been discovered not to work. The single most valuable field for an agent starting with no context.

authorizationScope.description: The concrete action being authorized, as structured data rather than a label. Replaces the ACP-1 string form deploy:staging: a string cannot be checked for having named an action at all.

authorizationLimits.description: Bounds on the worst case. At least one bound is required: an authorization with no limits is a blank cheque.

signal.description: The observation that would indicate this risk is materializing now. Without it a risk register is a list of worries.

authorized_by.description: Debt is a commitment of the programme's future capacity. An executor may propose it; only a role with scope authority may incur it.

gateSummary.description: Human-readable gate status per gate name. Informative: the authoritative evaluation is a validate event.

accept.description: Acceptance criteria another agent can execute without asking anything. Prose goals are not criteria.

allOf.$comment: A surface that claims everything defeats overlap detection, so it must be justified in the same event.

preempt_declaration.description: Taking over another agent's work requires two explicit statements, not an assumption.

claim.description: The claim event whose lease this renews (ACP-1.1, amendment A18). Without it, 'renew the lease' is a statement about a lease that is not named, and after a preemption nobody can tell which one.
The claim event whose lease this releases (amendment A18).

to.description: A specific actor, or any holder of a role. Handing back to a role pool is preferred: work addressed to a dead session is lost.

releases_lease.description: Explicit. A handoff that does not say so does not release the lease.

delivery.description: Delivery pointer. The enum is the NORMATIVE one of ACP-1.1 section 6.1. Schema 0.3.0 had unilaterally replaced it with a generic vocabulary (change-request, commit, artifact, external); that was the schema legislating over the specification, and it is reverted here. The generic vocabulary remains a proposal for ACP-1.2 and MUST NOT be anticipated. A pull request number still belongs in extensions.x-github-pr, not here.

allOf.$comment: Absence of evidence is admissible, but only as an explicit statement.

adversarial.description: Whether this review is adversarial under the active profile. Mandatory, and deliberately not optional: an optional flag could simply be omitted to escape the falsified requirement, whereas a mandatory one turns evasion into a signed false statement that the profile can contradict.

would_change_my_mind.description: The exit condition. Turns 'I do not like it' into something the executor can act on.

ev.revalidate.description: Reaffirms an earlier assertion across a SHA change. Distinct event type rather than a review field, so that old_basis, new_basis and the scope claim are all mandatory and machine-comparable.

outside_scope.description: True asserts the whole diff falls outside the reviewed scope. False requires naming what is being revalidated.

paths.description: The paths the diff actually touches. Non-empty (M3): a revalidation asserting that a diff falls outside the reviewed scope, while naming no path at all, asserts nothing checkable.

revalidated_claims.description: What was actually re-checked. Mandatory when the diff falls inside the reviewed scope.

unchanged_claims.description: Claims from the original assertion that this revalidation carries forward unchanged.

ev.authorize.description: Permission for an action with effects outside the repository. The strictest contract in the protocol.

not.$comment: Silence never authorizes. An authorization carrying a silent default would invert that rule.

unblock_when.description: A verifiable condition, so that anyone who checks it may lift the block.

workaround.description: Mandatory, and 'none' is a legitimate value. Forces the author to consider whether the block is real or merely tidier.

allOf.$comment: Silence never authorizes. For an authorization question the only admissible default is denial.

risk_if_wrong.description: A risk identifier or a description of the consequence.

ev.checkpoint.description: Bounds the reading obligation. Never removes history.

covers.description: Inclusive range of absorbed events: [first, last].

from.description: Protocol version this programme migrates FROM (ACP-1.1 section 16.4). Only on a programme checkpoint, and only together with to.

to.description: Protocol version this programme migrates TO. Only on a programme checkpoint, and only together with from.

allOf.$comment: H3: an item checkpoint summarises one item and carries that item's composite state and gate status. A programme checkpoint (ACP-1.1 sections 11.6 and 16.4) summarises a programme and has neither.
ACP-1.1 section 16.4: a major protocol change is announced by a PROGRAMME checkpoint declaring from and to.

after_multi.description: A reconciliation resolving a causal fork points at every branch it merges.

rule.$comment: The 23 codes of ACP-1.1 section 15.1, verbatim. Schema 0.3.0 carried only 15, which made eight violations that ACP-1.1 itself introduced impossible to report: identity-mismatch, unscoped-event, duplicate-root, dangling-pointer, alias-type, shadowed-field, malformed and missing-touches.

effect.description: void removes the denounced event's protocol effect; flag records it without disabling it.

carries.description: Risks and debt the item leaves behind. Closing without listing them is how they disappear.
